## Purpose

Try to use MOM6 data to calculate subsurface heatwaves in the California Current, taking advantage of the new earthmover setup for data access.

## Import Data

```{r setup,include=F}
library(rnaturalearth)
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(scales)
library(terra)
library(here)
library(tidyterra)
library(viridis)
library(colorspace)
library(tictoc)
library(cowplot)
library(corrplot)

theme_set(theme_minimal()+theme(panel.border = element_rect(color='black',fill=NA)))
```

Ocean heat content has been calculated separately in `calculate_ohc.R`. We calculated it across a bunch of depth bins: 0-5m, 0-50m, 50-100m, 100-250m, 250-500m, and 500-1000m depth.

```{r}
ohc1 <- rast(here('output','ocean_heat_content_0_5_ts.tif')) |> rotate()
ohc2 <- rast(here('output','ocean_heat_content_0_50_ts.tif')) |> rotate()
ohc3 <- rast(here('output','ocean_heat_content_50_100_ts.tif')) |> rotate()
ohc4 <- rast(here('output','ocean_heat_content_100_250_ts.tif')) |> rotate()
ohc5 <- rast(here('output','ocean_heat_content_250_500_ts.tif')) |> rotate()
ohc6 <- rast(here('output','ocean_heat_content_500_1000_ts.tif')) |> rotate()
ohcl <- list(ohc1,ohc2,ohc3,ohc4,ohc5,ohc6)
```

Background polygon

```{r,warning=F}
coast <- ne_states(country='United States of America',returnclass = 'sf') |> 
  filter(name %in% c('California','Oregon','Washington','Nevada',"Idaho"))
coastcn <- ne_countries(country="Canada",scale=50,returnclass='sf')

coast <- st_union(coast,coastcn) |> 
  summarise() |> 
  st_transform(st_crs(ohc1)) |>
  st_crop(st_bbox(ohc1))

# eez
eez <- read_sf(here('data','us_eez.shp')) |>
  st_transform(st_crs(ohc1)) |> 
  st_crop(st_bbox(ohc1))

```


## Calculate Anomalies

Calculate a monthly climatology. Crop everything to the eez

```{r}
ohc_climl <- map(ohcl,\(x) tapp(x,index='months',fun=mean) |> mask(vect(eez)))
ohc_clim_sdl <- map(ohcl,\(x) tapp(x,index='months',fun=sd) |> mask(vect(eez)))
```

```{r}
names(ohc_climl) <- c("0-5","0-50","50-100","100-250","250-500","500-1000")

panel(ohc_climl[[1]],col=map.pal("bcyr"))
panel(ohc_climl[[2]],col=map.pal("bcyr"))
```

Try counting anomalies from these climatologies. We define anomaly as a z-score anomaly, that is, we substract the mean and divide by the standard deviation.

```{r}
# split into months, subtract climatology, recombine
# anoml2 <- map2(ohcl,ohc_climl, \(x,y) x - y)
anoml <- pmap(list(ohcl,ohc_climl,ohc_clim_sdl), \(x,y,z) (x - y)/z)
names(anoml) <- c("0-5","0-50","50-100","100-250","250-500","500-1000")
# names(anom) <- time(anom)
```

Try plotting all months from 2013-2016 (the Blob).

```{r}
blobp_foo <- function(rstack){

  ggplot()+
    geom_spatraster(data=rstack)+
    geom_sf(data=coast,fill="tan",color=NA)+
    geom_sf(data=eez,fill=NA,color='black',linetype=2)+

                                    na.value='gray90',limits=c(-2,4))+

    # scale_fill_continuous(palette=paldiv,oob=oob_squish,limits=c(-2.5,2.5))+
    labs(title="Ocean Heat Content",
         fill='Anomaly')+
    theme(axis.text.x=element_blank(),axis.text.y=element_text(size=8))
}

times <- time(ohc2)
ss <- which(year(times)%in%c(2013:2016))
blobtl <- iwalk(anoml,\(x,y){
  p <- blobp_foo(x[[ss]])
  ggsave(here('plots',paste0('Blob OHC ts_',y,'.png')),p,h=24)
})
```

## Detrending

Let's make de-trended versions of the rasters, removing any linear effect of time on the anomalies. This will help us distinguish, e.g., short term deviations (heatwaves) from long-term warming.

```{r}
extract_trend <- function(rast_series, time_index=1:nlyr(rast_series)) {
  t_idx <- time_index
  
  trend <- app(rast_series, function(x) {
    if (all(is.na(x))) return(rep(NA, length(x)))
    fit <- lm(x ~ t_idx)
    return(fitted(fit))
  })
  
  return(trend)
}

trendl <- map(anoml,extract_trend)
detrendl <- map2(anoml,trendl,\(x,y) x-y)
```

```{r}
# not just the fitted values-- what are the spatial time trends?
extract_trend_coef <- function(rast_series, time_index=1:nlyr(rast_series)) {
  t_idx <- time_index
  
  trend <- app(rast_series, function(x) {
    if (all(is.na(x))) return(NA)
    fit <- lm(x ~ t_idx)
    return(coef(fit)[2])
  })
  
  return(trend)
}
test <- map(anoml,extract_trend_coef)
```

## Anomaly timeseries

Can we use this dataset to calculate a timeseries? First, a simple mean anomaly over time, averaging the anomaly values across all grid cells in a given time step and depth layer.

```{r}
timetbl <- tibble(date=time(ohc1)) |> 
  mutate(year=year(date),month=month(date))

# list of anomaly timeseries, for each depth bin
anom_ts <- imap(anoml,\(x,i) {
  global(x,c("mean","sd"),na.rm=T) |>
    bind_cols(timetbl) |> 
    mutate(upr=mean+1.96*sd,lwr=mean-1.96*sd,
           depth_layer=i)
  }) |> bind_rows()

ohc_ts <- imap(ohcl,\(x,i){
  global(x,c("mean","sd"),na.rm=T) |>
    bind_cols(timetbl) |> 
    mutate(upr=mean+1.96*sd,lwr=mean-1.96*sd,
           depth_layer=i)
}) |> bind_rows()


p_anom_ts <- anom_ts |> 
  mutate(depthcat=factor(depth_layer,levels=c("0-5","0-50","50-100","100-250","250-500","500-1000"))) |>
  # filter(depth_layer==2) |>
  # filter(year<2025) |> 
  ggplot(aes(date,mean,ymin=lwr,ymax=upr,color=depthcat,
             fill=depthcat))+
  geom_ribbon(alpha=0.5,col=NA)+
  geom_line()+
  scale_fill_manual(values=viridis_pal(begin=0.3,end=0.7)(6))+
  scale_color_manual(values=viridis_pal(begin=0.3,end=0.7)(6))+
  geom_hline(yintercept=0,linetype=2)+
  scale_x_date(date_breaks="3 years",date_labels="%Y")+
  labs(x="Year",y="OHC Anomaly")+
  guides(fill='none',col='none')+
  facet_wrap(~depthcat,nrow=2)+
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45,hjust=1,vjust=1))
p_anom_ts

p_ohc_ts <- ohc_ts |> 
  # filter(depth_layer==2) |>
  # filter(year<2025) |> 
  ggplot(aes(date,mean,ymin=lwr,ymax=upr,color=factor(depth_layer),
             fill=factor(depth_layer)))+
  geom_ribbon(alpha=0.5,col=NA)+
  geom_line()+
  scale_fill_manual(values=viridis_pal(begin=0.3,end=0.7)(6))+
  scale_color_manual(values=viridis_pal(begin=0.3,end=0.7)(6))+
  scale_x_date(date_breaks="3 years",date_labels="%Y")+
  labs(x="Year",y="OHC",fill="Depth\nLayer",col="Depth\nLayer")+
  facet_wrap(~factor(depth_layer),nrow=2,scales='free')+
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45,hjust=1,vjust=1))
p_ohc_ts
```

## By Latitude

We can also make time series by latitude bins, to assess any latitudinal differences in the timing or magnitude of ocean heat changes.

```{r}
# make latitude bin raster
lat_rast <- anoml[[1]][[1]]  # Get one layer as template
values(lat_rast) <- NA
# Fill with latitude bin IDs
lat_breaks <- seq(32, 50, by=2)  # 2° bins
lat_labels <- paste(lat_breaks+1, "°N", sep = "")
zonetbl <- tibble(minlat=lat_breaks,maxlat=lead(lat_breaks)) |> 
                    mutate(zone=row_number())

# assign latitude bin ids to each raster cell
for (i in 1:nrow(lat_rast)) {
  cell_lat <- yFromCell(lat_rast, cellFromRowCol(lat_rast, i,1))
  bin_id <- cut(cell_lat, breaks=lat_breaks, labels=FALSE)
  lat_rast[i, ] <- bin_id
}
```

Or by HCI regions

```{r}
# Fill with latitude bin IDs
hci_breaks <- c(30, 35.5,40,43.5,48)  # 2° bins
hci_labels <- paste(hci_breaks, "°N", sep = "")
hcitbl <- tibble(minlat=hci_breaks,maxlat=lead(hci_breaks)) |> 
                    mutate(hci_region=c(5:1))

# assign bin ids to each raster cell
hci_rast <- anoml[[1]][[1]]  # Get one layer as template
for (i in 1:nrow(hci_rast)) {
  cell_lat <- yFromCell(hci_rast, cellFromRowCol(hci_rast, i,1))
  bin_id <- cut(cell_lat, breaks=hci_breaks)
  hci_rast[i, ] <- bin_id
}
hci_rast <- 5-hci_rast # swap the order of the HCI regions
```

Use the latitude bin template raster and `terra::zonal()` to calculate latitude-bin means for all depth layers.

```{r}
# for each depth layer...
ts_by_lat <- imap(anoml,\(x,idx){
  # and for each time slice...
  imap(1:nlyr(x), \(t,n) {
    # ...calculate the mean anomaly value by latitude bin
    ldf <- zonal(x[[t]], lat_rast, fun="mean",na.rm=T, as.data.frame=TRUE)
    tibble(date=n,zone=ldf[,1],mean=ldf[,2])
    }) |> bind_rows() |> 
    mutate(depth_layer=idx)
}) |> bind_rows() |> 
  mutate(depthcat=factor(depth_layer,levels=c("0-5","0-50","50-100","100-250","250-500","500-1000")))

# detrended version
ts_by_lat_det <- imap(detrendl,\(x,idx){
  imap(1:nlyr(x), \(t,n) {
    ldf <- zonal(x[[t]], lat_rast, fun="mean",na.rm=T, as.data.frame=TRUE)
    tibble(date=n,zone=ldf[,1],mean=ldf[,2])
    }) |> bind_rows() |> 
    mutate(depth_layer=idx)
}) |> bind_rows() |> 
  mutate(depthcat=factor(depth_layer,levels=c("0-5","0-50","50-100","100-250","250-500","500-1000")))
```

Plot the time series by latitude bin.


## By HCI Region

Use the HCI template raster and `terra::zonal()` to calculate HCI-region means for all depth layers.

```{r}
# for each depth layer...
ts_by_hci <- imap(anoml,\(x,idx){
  # and for each time slice...
  imap(1:nlyr(x), \(t,n) {
    # ...calculate the mean anomaly value by latitude bin
    ldf <- zonal(x[[t]], hci_rast, fun="mean",na.rm=T, as.data.frame=TRUE)
    tibble(date=n,zone=ldf[,1],mean=ldf[,2])
    }) |> bind_rows() |> 
    mutate(depth_layer=idx)
}) |> bind_rows() |> 
  mutate(depthcat=factor(depth_layer,levels=c("0-5","0-50","50-100","100-250","250-500","500-1000")))

# detrended version
ts_by_hci_det <- imap(detrendl,\(x,idx){
  imap(1:nlyr(x), \(t,n) {
    ldf <- zonal(x[[t]], hci_rast, fun="mean",na.rm=T, as.data.frame=TRUE)
    tibble(date=n,zone=ldf[,1],mean=ldf[,2])
    }) |> bind_rows() |> 
    mutate(depth_layer=idx)
}) |> bind_rows() |> 
  mutate(depthcat=factor(depth_layer,levels=c("0-5","0-50","50-100","100-250","250-500","500-1000")))
```

### Correlations

Correlations of this time series among regions and depths.

```{r}
# make into wide form
ts_hci_wide <- ts_by_hci |>
  mutate(series = paste(zone, depth_layer, sep = "|")) |>
  group_by(date, series) |>
  summarise(value = mean(mean, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>  # guards against duplicate dates
  pivot_wider(names_from = series, values_from = value) |>
  arrange(date)

# function to test correlations, with adjustment for effective sample size
pair_cor <- function(x, y) {
  ok <- complete.cases(x, y); x <- x[ok]; y <- y[ok]; n <- length(x)
  r   <- cor(x, y)
  r1x <- acf(x, lag.max = 1, plot = FALSE)$acf[2]
  r1y <- acf(y, lag.max = 1, plot = FALSE)$acf[2]
  neff <- n * (1 - r1x * r1y) / (1 + r1x * r1y)
  neff <- min(max(neff, 3.1), n)
  t <- r * sqrt((neff - 2) / (1 - r^2))
  tibble(r = r, n = n, neff = neff, p = 2 * pt(-abs(t), neff - 2))
}

series <- setdiff(names(ts_hci_wide), "date")

# for every combination of zone and depth, calculate correlations
cors <- combn(series, 2, simplify = FALSE) |>
  map_dfr(\(p) bind_cols(a = p[1], b = p[2], pair_cor(ts_hci_wide[[p[1]]], ts_hci_wide[[p[2]]]))) |>
  separate(a, c("zone_a", "depth_a"), sep = "\\|") |>
  separate(b, c("zone_b", "depth_b"), sep = "\\|") |>
  mutate(comparison = case_when(
    depth_a == depth_b & zone_a != zone_b ~ "zones within depth layer",
    zone_a  == zone_b  & depth_a != depth_b ~ "depth layers within zone",
    TRUE ~ "both differ"))

# adjustment for multiple comparison
cors <- cors |>
  group_by(comparison) |>
  mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")) |>
  ungroup()
```


Make a plot of the correlations

```{r}
cm <- cor(ts_hci_wide[series], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
# ordered by region and depth
corrplot::corrplot(cm, method = "color", order = "alphabet", tl.cex = 0.6)

# clustered for easier viewing
corrplot::corrplot(cm, method = "color", order = "hclust", tl.cex = 0.6)

# 2. Open the PNG graphics device
png(filename = here('plots',"ohc_hci_regions_corrplot.png"), 
    width = 1800, 
    height = 1800, 
    res = 300,        # High resolution (300 DPI) for print
    type = "cairo")   # Ensures sharp labels and smooth lines
corrplot::corrplot(cm, method = "color", order = "hclust", tl.cex = 0.6)
dev.off()
```

## Heatwave Area

We can also calculate heatwave area. In our case, we'll define heatwave area as the total (summed) area of any grid cells in a given time step that have an anomaly value  greater than 1; that is, the total area greater than 1 SD above the long-term, monthly climatology.

```{r}
# terra calculates area correctly even with lat/lon coordinates,
# so we can just pull the area of each raster cell (which is in meters)
# and convert to sq. km
rarea <- cellSize(anoml[[1]])/1e6

calc_heatwave_area <- function(r,thresh=1){
  # find the area of all cells in heatwave
  rna <- ifel(r<thresh,NA,r)
  expanse(rna,unit='km') |> pull(area)
}

# Total area key (for calculating percent of region)
tot_areas_z <- map_dbl(anoml,\(x){
  expanse(x[[1]]) |> pull(area)
})/1e6 # convert to sq. km
tot_area_df <- tibble(layer=names(tot_areas_z),totarea=tot_areas_z)
tot_area_df |> 
  mutate(layer=factor(layer,levels=names(tot_areas_z))) |> 
  ggplot(aes(layer,totarea))+geom_col()+
  labs(y="Total Area (sq. km)",x="Depth Layer")
```

```{r}

  area <- sapply(x,calc_heatwave_area,thresh=1)
  tibble(date=timetbl$date,area=unlist(area),
         depth_layer=y)
}) |> bind_rows()

  area <- sapply(x,calc_heatwave_area,thresh=1)

}) |> bind_rows()
```

## Consistent Spatial Pattern

Find areas that consistently are affected by heatwave conditions, in total and by month. First we look at frequency- how many months did each pixel exceed the threshold of 1SD above the climatological mean?

```{r}
# find the frequency that each cell exceeds threshold
threshold= 1
hwfreqtot <- map(anoml,\(x){
  out <- app(x,\(y) sum(y>threshold,na.rm=T))
  ifel(out<=0,NA,out)
})
hwfreqmonth <- map(anoml,\(x){
  out <- tapp(x,"months",\(y) sum(y>threshold,na.rm=T))
  ifel(out<=0,NA,out)
})
```

Areas with sustained heatwaves (consecutive months exceeding threshold)

```{r}
threshold=1 # threshold for heatwave conditions (in anomaly space, so 1SD)
duration_threshold=4 # number of consecutive months needed to call it a heatwave
consecutive_heatwaves <- map(anoml,\(x){
  out <- app(x, \(y) {
    # Find indices where x > threshold
    is_hw <- y > threshold
    
    # Calculate run lengths of TRUE values
    runs <- rle(is_hw)
    
    # Count number of runs lasting > 3 months (sustained heatwaves)
    persistent <- sum(runs$lengths[runs$values] > duration_threshold, na.rm = TRUE)
    
    return(persistent)
  })
  out
  # ifel(out <= 0,NA,out)
})
```

```{r,fig.width=10}
p_hwsus1 <- ggplot()+
  geom_spatraster(data=rast(consecutive_heatwaves))+
  geom_sf(data=coast,fill="tan")+
  facet_wrap(~lyr)+
  geom_sf(data=eez,fill=NA,color="black")+
  scale_fill_viridis(option='turbo',breaks=seq(0,10,by=2),oob=oob_squish)+
  scale_x_continuous(expand=c(0,0))+
  scale_y_continuous(expand=c(0,0))+
  labs(title="Areas with sustained heatwaves\nlasting >4 consecutive months",
       fill='Number of Heatwaves')+
  theme(axis.text.x=element_blank())
p_hwsus1
```

## Breakpoint Analysis

Using the time series of OHC anomalies, test for breakpoints. Here's a general function to test all plausible breakpoint months using 3 different possible breakpoint models: a piecewise but continuous linear, a discontinuous linear, or a mean shift.

```{r}
# df has columns with time index (tidx) and y (value of interest)
fit_break <- function(depthcat, type = c("mean", "trend_disc", "trend_cont"), trim = 0.15) {
  type <- match.arg(type)
  
  df <- anom_ts |> 
    filter(depth_layer==depthcat) |> 
    arrange(date) |> 
    mutate(tidx=row_number(),y=mean)
  
  tx  <- sort(unique(df$tidx))
  n    <- length(tx)
  
  # keep >= trim of data per side
  cand <- tx[ceiling(trim * n):floor((1 - trim) * n)]  
  
  # fit model for all possible breakpoints
  mk <- function(bp) switch(type,
    mean       = lm(y ~ I(tidx > bp), data = df),
    trend_disc = lm(y ~ tidx * I(tidx > bp), data = df),
    trend_cont = lm(y ~ tidx + pmax(tidx - bp, 0), data = df))

  fits <- lapply(cand, mk)
  rss  <- vapply(fits, deviance, numeric(1))
  best <- which.min(rss)

  # Approximate 95% CI for the breakpoint: candidates whose RSS is not
  # significantly worse than the best (likelihood-ratio style)
  lr  <- nrow(df) * log(rss / rss[best])
  ci  <- range(cand[lr <= qchisq(0.95, 1)])
  
  fit = fits[[best]]
  bp = cand[[best]]
  
  bplab <- df$date[which(df$tidx==bp)]
  # plot the output
  p <- df |> 
    mutate(pred=predict(fit)) |>
    mutate(group=ifelse(tidx<=bp,"Before","After")) |> 
    ggplot(aes(x=date))+
    geom_line(aes(y=pred,color=group),linetype=2,linewidth = 1.5)+
    geom_line(aes(y=mean))+
    guides(color='none')+
    labs(title=paste("Breakpoint:",bplab,"\n",paste0(depthcat,"m")),color="",y="OHC Anomaly")

  
  out <- list(bp = cand[best], ci = ci, fit = fits[[best]],
       profile = data.frame(bp = cand, rss = rss), type = type,
       plot=p)
  out
  
}
```

Using the top (surface) depth layer, test the breakpoint calculations.

```{r}
# test a mean shift
res <- fit_break(depthcat = "0-5", type="mean")
res$bp; res$ci
summary(res$fit)
# Was the breakpoint well-identified?  check for a sharp vs. flat minimum on the RSS plot
plot(res$profile, type = "l") 

res$plot
```

Test a continuous linear with one breakpoint

```{r}
res <- fit_break(depthcat = "0-5", type="trend_cont")
res$bp; res$ci
summary(res$fit)
# Was the breakpoint well-identified?  check for a sharp vs. flat minimum on the RSS plot
plot(res$profile, type = "l") 

res$plot
```
And finally, a piecewise, discontinuous linear

```{r}
res <- fit_break(depthcat = "0-5", type="trend_disc")
res$bp; res$ci
summary(res$fit)
# Was the breakpoint well-identified?  check for a sharp vs. flat minimum on the RSS plot
plot(res$profile, type = "l") 

res$plot
```

Really interesting that both the mean shift and the discontinous linear identify February, 2014 as the month of the "regime shift" into the new MHW era.

Let's try this for all the depth layers, using the discontinuous linear.

```{r}
bp_all <- map(names(anoml),\(x){
  fit_break(depthcat = x, type="trend_disc")
})
p_bp <- map(bp_all,\(y) y$plot)

cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist=p_bp,nrow=2)

ggsave(here('plots','breakpoint_analysis.png'),cowplot::plot_grid(plotlist=p_bp,nrow=2),w=10,h=7)
```

We can try to do the same breakpoint analysis with the area-normalized time series.

```{r}
fit_break_area <- function(depthcat, type = c("mean", "trend_disc", "trend_cont"), trim = 0.15) {
  type <- match.arg(type)
  
  df <- heatwave_area_ts |> 
    filter(depth_layer==depthcat) |> 
    arrange(date) |> 
    mutate(tidx=row_number(),y=prop)
  
  tx  <- sort(unique(df$tidx))
  n    <- length(tx)
  
  # keep >= trim of data per side
  cand <- tx[ceiling(trim * n):floor((1 - trim) * n)]  
  
  # fit model for all possible breakpoints
  mk <- function(bp) switch(type,
    mean       = lm(y ~ I(tidx > bp), data = df),
    trend_disc = lm(y ~ tidx * I(tidx > bp), data = df),
    trend_cont = lm(y ~ tidx + pmax(tidx - bp, 0), data = df))

  fits <- lapply(cand, mk)
  rss  <- vapply(fits, deviance, numeric(1))
  best <- which.min(rss)

  # Approximate 95% CI for the breakpoint: candidates whose RSS is not
  # significantly worse than the best (likelihood-ratio style)
  lr  <- nrow(df) * log(rss / rss[best])
  ci  <- range(cand[lr <= qchisq(0.95, 1)])
  
  fit = fits[[best]]
  bp = cand[[best]]
  
  bplab <- df$date[which(df$tidx==bp)]
  # plot the output
  p <- df |> 
    mutate(pred=predict(fit)) |>
    mutate(group=ifelse(tidx<=bp,"Before","After")) |> 
    ggplot(aes(x=date))+
    geom_line(aes(y=pred,color=group),linetype=2,linewidth = 1.5)+
    geom_line(aes(y=prop))+
    guides(color='none')+
    labs(title=paste("Breakpoint:",bplab,"\n",paste0(depthcat,"m")),color="",y="Propotion in Heatwave Conditions")

  
  out <- list(bp = cand[best], ci = ci, fit = fits[[best]],
       profile = data.frame(bp = cand, rss = rss), type = type,
       plot=p)
  out
  
}
```

Run a mean-shift breakpoint analysis on the area time series

```{r}
  fit_break_area(depthcat = x, type="mean")
})
```
